A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TASE work, and all 19 pages of each support comparison of text, equations, figures and tables. Both end with references; neither includes the supplement mentioned in the text, so no appendix content was available to compare.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-editing experiments, user-study outcomes in Table 1, component ablations in Table 2, and qualitative results in Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental and user-study results, adds two quantitative baseline comparisons, and reports revised editing scores in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The embedding training, equivariance loss, feature lifting, segmentation, ControlNet finetuning and editing procedures remain unchanged. Table 2 relabels Leqv as Lcons, but the method equations and explanation retain Leqv; this does not establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet-1k training, local object editing, global weather and lighting edits, and conditional image-generation examples at different truncation levels. No additional dataset, population or distinct test scenario is documented.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially broadens the central quantitative comparison by adding DreamCatalyst and EditSplat alongside DGE and the same GaussianEditor previously abbreviated GE. EditSplat becomes the closest reported competitor. The qualitative comparison and user study retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: The documented training budgets, model configurations, evaluation metrics and held-out reconstruction evaluation remain unchanged. Neither PDF states a protocol revision explaining the replacement CLIP scores, and v2 supplies no additional evaluation settings for the new baselines.

E4.justification: Table 2 revises quantitative evidence for the existing dimensionality-reduction, equivariance-loss and finetuning ablations. TASE with the loss but without finetuning now slightly exceeds PCA with finetuning, reversing their previous ordering. The six configurations, questions tested and qualitative ablation examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for these comparisons. Tables 1–2 continue to report point estimates and user-preference percentages without added uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces GaussianEditor, DGE and TASE CLIP scores from 0.0493, 0.0574 and 0.1014 to 0.1179, 0.1247 and 0.1542, respectively, and adds DreamCatalyst at 0.0985 and EditSplat at 0.1492. All six Table 2 CLIP scores also change; PCA+FT versus TASE+loss changes from 0.0941 versus 0.0925 to 0.1365 versus 0.1385. User-study percentages and reconstruction results remain unchanged apart from SSIM rounding. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–16 are unchanged, with no added assumptions, derivations or proofs. The isolated Lcons label in Table 2 introduces no new mathematical definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about controllable semantic abstraction, cross-view consistency, substantial geometric edits and diffusion finetuning. The expanded comparison does not accompany a revised core claim.

C2.justification: The explanations of positional bias, PCA geometry failures and finetuning benefits are retained. The limitations concerning densification tuning, stochastic artifacts and entangled semantics and appearance also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 retains the same implementation details, learning rates, channel dimensions, training epochs and 50,000 finetuning pairs. No new hardware, runtime, code-access information or instructions explaining the revised scores are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DreamCatalyst reference and comparison. EditSplat was already cited in v1 and now participates in Table 1. The related-work discussion and broader positioning otherwise remain unchanged; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to table captions and labels, including expanding GE to GaussianEditor and changing 'equivariance loss Leqv' to 'consistency loss Lcons' in Table 2. The main prose and section organization remain intact, leaving the new loss terminology inconsistent with the surrounding text.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and a revised caption. Table 2 replaces shared reconstruction cells with values on the unfinetuned rows and dashes on the finetuned rows, and reduces SSIM precision. These changes cause local text reflow; all six figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: Adding DreamCatalyst and EditSplat provides useful comparative context, especially the close EditSplat–TASE scores of 0.1492 and 0.1542. However, v2 replaces every CLIP score in Tables 1–2 without explaining the computational or experimental basis and introduces inconsistent loss terminology in Table 2. The PDFs do not establish whether the numerical revisions improve the evidence's accuracy or comparability, preventing a reliable judgment of net paper-quality improvement.
